exam_guide_revision: Not a certification. Practical Python 3.10-3.14 fluency track; official Python documentation and selected AnyIO/HTTPX docs reviewed 2026-09-19.

learning_design.unlock_rule: A knowledge node unlocks after all required prompts are revealed.
learning_design.mastery_note: Discovery progress is not mastery evidence; progressively harder typed code recall provides the scored signal.

authoring_notes: Python Fluency is practical coding retrieval, not beginner trivia or a certification. Questions use progressive recall depth: guided -> recall -> construct -> fluency. Short literals stay on one line where readable, unfamiliar data shapes and intent are explained, and most questions have one meaningful blank.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ lazily presents multiple iterables as one continuous iterator without first concatenating them into a new list.

reveal.text: itertools.chain lazily presents multiple iterables as one continuous iterator without first concatenating them into a new list.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ item in chain(primary, fallback): ... consumes primary then fallback.

reveal.text: for item in chain(primary, fallback): ... consumes primary then fallback.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________(groups) is preferable when the iterables themselves already live in another iterable.

reveal.text: chain.from_iterable(groups) is preferable when the iterables themselves already live in another iterable.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(iterable, n) lazily groups input items into tuples of up to n elements.

reveal.text: itertools.batched(iterable, n) lazily groups input items into tuples of up to n elements.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ batch in batched(records, 100): insert(batch) processes fixed-size chunks without manual slicing.

reveal.text: for batch in batched(records, 100): insert(batch) processes fixed-size chunks without manual slicing.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ Python 3.13's strict option, the final batch may be shorter; code requiring exact batch size must account for that.

reveal.text: Before Python 3.13's strict option, the final batch may be shorter; code requiring exact batch size must account for that.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(iterable) yields overlapping adjacent pairs such as (x0, x1), (x1, x2), and so on.

reveal.text: itertools.pairwise(iterable) yields overlapping adjacent pairs such as (x0, x1), (x1, x2), and so on.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ previous, current in pairwise(values): ... compares neighbors without manual indexing.

reveal.text: for previous, current in pairwise(values): ... compares neighbors without manual indexing.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ yields nothing for fewer than two input elements, so code expecting at least one pair must handle short input.

reveal.text: pairwise yields nothing for fewer than two input elements, so code expecting at least one pair must handle short input.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(func, iterable_of_args) calls func(*args) for each tuple-like argument group from the iterable.

reveal.text: itertools.starmap(func, iterable_of_args) calls func(*args) for each tuple-like argument group from the iterable.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(pow, [(2, 5), (3, 2)]) applies pow to each argument tuple lazily.

reveal.text: starmap(pow, [(2, 5), (3, 2)]) applies pow to each argument tuple lazily.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ map() when each input item is one argument; use starmap() when each input item should be expanded into multiple positional arguments.

reveal.text: Use map() when each input item is one argument; use starmap() when each input item should be expanded into multiple positional arguments.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ overloads / for path joining and provides object-oriented methods for reading, writing, globbing, and path transformations.

reveal.text: pathlib.Path overloads / for path joining and provides object-oriented methods for reading, writing, globbing, and path transformations.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = base / 'config' / 'app.json' avoids manual separator handling.

reveal.text: config_path = base / 'config' / 'app.json' avoids manual separator handling.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ objects represent filesystem paths, not guaranteed-existing files; existence and file type still need explicit checks when required.

reveal.text: Path objects represent filesystem paths, not guaranteed-existing files; existence and file type still need explicit checks when required.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________() is the recommended high-level API for executing a child process and waiting for it to finish.

reveal.text: subprocess.run() is the recommended high-level API for executing a child process and waiting for it to finish.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True) raises on a non-zero exit and returns decoded stdout/stderr.

reveal.text: subprocess.run(cmd, check=True, capture_output=True, text=True) raises on a non-zero exit and returns decoded stdout/stderr.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ an argument list over shell=True for ordinary commands; shell parsing adds quoting complexity and can create injection risk with untrusted input.

reveal.text: Prefer an argument list over shell=True for ordinary commands; shell parsing adds quoting complexity and can create injection risk with untrusted input.

modules.title: Use dates, JSON, heaps, and bisect

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(timezone.utc) creates an aware UTC datetime whose tzinfo is explicit.

reveal.text: datetime.now(timezone.utc) creates an aware UTC datetime whose tzinfo is explicit.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ datetime.now(timezone.utc) for an aware UTC timestamp rather than a naive datetime.utcnow().

reveal.text: Use datetime.now(timezone.utc) for an aware UTC timestamp rather than a naive datetime.utcnow().

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ naive and aware datetimes leads to ambiguous semantics and can raise during comparisons.

reveal.text: Mixing naive and aware datetimes leads to ambiguous semantics and can raise during comparisons.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(..., default=callable) invokes the callable for otherwise non-serializable objects so application-specific conversion can be defined.

reveal.text: json.dumps(..., default=callable) invokes the callable for otherwise non-serializable objects so application-specific conversion can be defined.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(payload, default=str) is a simple fallback when converting unsupported objects to strings is intentionally acceptable.

reveal.text: json.dumps(payload, default=str) is a simple fallback when converting unsupported objects to strings is intentionally acceptable.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________=str can hide accidental unsupported types; a stricter custom encoder is often better when representation matters.

reveal.text: default=str can hide accidental unsupported types; a stricter custom encoder is often better when representation matters.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________(n, iterable, key=...) returns the n largest items without sorting the entire input when n is relatively small.

reveal.text: heapq.nlargest(n, iterable, key=...) returns the n largest items without sorting the entire input when n is relatively small.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________ = nlargest(10, users, key=lambda u: u.score) directly returns the ten highest-scoring users.

reveal.text: top = nlargest(10, users, key=lambda u: u.score) directly returns the ten highest-scoring users.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ large n relative to input size, sorted(..., reverse=True) may be simpler and can be competitive.

reveal.text: For large n relative to input size, sorted(..., reverse=True) may be simpler and can be competitive.

prompts.label: ❓ WHAT?
prompts.placeholder: __________ keeps a list sorted by locating an insertion point with binary search and then inserting the value.

reveal.text: bisect.insort keeps a list sorted by locating an insertion point with binary search and then inserting the value.

prompts.label: ⌨️ CODE?
prompts.placeholder: __________(scores, new_score) is convenient when maintaining a small sorted list incrementally.

reveal.text: insort(scores, new_score) is convenient when maintaining a small sorted list incrementally.

prompts.label: ⚠️ GOTCHA
prompts.placeholder: __________ the index is logarithmic, but list insertion is still O(n) because later elements must be shifted.

reveal.text: Finding the index is logarithmic, but list insertion is still O(n) because later elements must be shifted.
